I would mostly see them when they were driving around. Another thing that was characteristic was that they would usually drive a little faster than normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if I understood your testimony earlier correctly, you have lived in the area near Mehurici, Zagradje, for most of your life?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during the 11 years that you were a teacher in Mehurici, you obviously encountered hundreds of students.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if I did my math right, you stopped being a teacher in the school in Mehurici approximately 1990?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. I stopped working in late 1990 at the Mehurici school. In 1991, I spent a great deal of time in Nasice with my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me return to a topic that you mentioned several times today, and that is the local Bosniak men who joined the Mujahedin. Do you recall or can you tell us approximately how many Bosniak men affiliated themselves with the Mujahedin in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the settlement itself, Mehurici and the areas close by, there weren't that many. Maybe about ten or 12, as far as I know. This is in the -- in Mehurici itself and the areas that are closest to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than these ten or 12 people, did you become aware or know of any local Bosniaks from outside the immediate area who affiliated themselves with the Mujahedin in Mehurici or in the Mehurici environs?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Of course. As I was living there, I heard and I learned, had information to that effect, that a certain number of people joined the Mujahedin from the area of Han Bila. But it's interesting that a considerable number of people who had been expelled or had fled from other areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina and who came to the area of the Travnik municipality, and specifically to the Bila valley area, had joined the Mujahedin. What their reasons were they would know best, but I know that these were people who had previously been expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you also told us earlier that of the ten to 12 local Bosniaks who joined the Mujahedin, you knew some of them and actually inquired of them why they had affiliated themselves with the Mujahedin. Your answer was that they were offered uniforms and weapons by the Mujahedin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. That was their response to my question why they had joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of these ten to 12 people that you spoke with who affiliated themselves with the Mujahedin? And if you don't feel comfortable saying that in public, we can certainly go into private session for you to do so.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I really couldn't recall the names of all ten right now, but I could remember some names. I've forgotten most of the names, but perhaps if I thought about it a little bit more, perhaps I could remember some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sitting here now, sir, do you remember the names of one or two or three or any of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I remember a young man who approached me at the time during the Miletici case. His name was Adnan Pasanovic. He stayed with them, completed the training, and then he later rejoined the BH army. He returned to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of anyone else?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I remember a person. His last name is Jasarevic. I can't remember his first name. This is a man who is working, Jasarevic. I also recall a person whose last name was Celam. I cannot remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you know the names of Osman Tahirovic.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. I know Osman Tahirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did Osman Tahirovic affiliate with the Mujahedin in Mehurici in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, you could see that he was cooperating with them. I know that together with another man, he worked in a cafe where they would drop by to drink coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Rather than drinking -- or stopping by to drink coffee, did Osman Tahirovic affiliate himself or receive any training or uniforms from the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I don't know personally what his particular relationship was with them in that sense of belonging or uniforms. I know, though, that when they were staying at the school, he worked as a cook or something like that for them, and that's how I would see him in the same places that they would frequent, in that cafe and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if at any point in 1993 Osman Tahirovic was a member of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, because the population of Zagradje was mostly in the 314th Unit, which was holding the positions in the area facing Teslic. So I really don't know. I can't remember. I do not know whether at the time he was a member of that unit together with the others from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if at any point in time in the second half of 1992 if Osman Tahirovic was a member of the Muslimanske Snage in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me return to the general issue of Bosniaks affiliating with the Mujahedin. Do you know an individual by the name of Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I would see him in Mehurici. As far as I knew at the time, he was born in Zenica, and I think he was one of the first to join the Mujahedin in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if at any point in time Ramo Durmis was a member of the ABiH 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know whether Ramo Durmis went by any other names or nicknames?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that personally. I knew him by sight. I would see him, for example, when he passed through Mehurici. So no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know if Ramo Durmis was married to a woman from Maline?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know an individual by the name of Emsud Karadzic [sic], and do you know if he had any affiliation with the Mujahedin? I note in the transcript it says "Karadzic." The name is Kadiric. Emsud Kadiric.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: It is the first time I've heard of this name. I don't know such a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me turn to the topic of the Mujahedin camp. Do you know specifically where this camp was that was in the immediate vicinity of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because you can see it with the naked eye. It's at the edge of Mehurici, between 500 and 800 metres, and that's where the Savici settlement was located. The population, up until 1991, was mainly Serbian. And when they arrived in the school and left the school, they entered that village, and that is where they formed the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where is the Savici settlement in relation to Poljanice?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Savici, in relation to Poljanice, is to the south-east, but it's very close. The fields, the land, link up the two villages. It's just the land that belongs to the people living there that separates the two villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I'm going to show the witness a map. And I don't know if these locations are on here, but I would certainly ask that the witness mark these places if he's able to see them on the map. And I do have sufficient copies. It's simply part of the rather large map that we've been using that's mounted. I would ask that that be placed on the ELMO, please, and that the witness be provided with a thin marker if that's possible. I think the thick ones might be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, before marking anything, I would ask you first to take a look at this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if the usher could please centre it a little bit better. We're actually looking at the upper-left corner of the map. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, before making any marks, let me ask you if you see the location where the Savici settlement is on this map.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First, if you could point to it, please, and then I'll ask you to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps the AV booth could, I don't know, focus that a little bit better or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's more or less here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, if you could then take the black marker, the thin black marker that the usher will provide you with, and if you could circle the area representing the Savici settlement?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps to the -- to the immediate right of that, if you could write the word "Savici."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, it was in the location that you've just circled where the Mujahedin had their training camp?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. That's where they were. That's where the camp was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, while we have this map, let me ask you a couple of other questions relating to some areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if the usher could move that map down just a little bit or -- actually, up, the other direction. A little bit more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it may not be on here, sir, but can you see, and again using the pointer before making any marks, do you see the Luka area of Zagradje on this map and, if so, could you please point to that on this map?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: This is where Luka is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If you could again take the thin, black marker, circle the Luka settlement.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps a little bit below that and maybe to the right if you could write the word "Luka."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you also told us on the -- I believe it was the 24th but correct me if I'm mistaken. The 24th of April, 1993, you saw a column of villagers being taken somewhere by the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: At dusk, we were involved in discussions concerning someone arriving from the command of the unit while they were being taken through Mehurici. This is where the bridge is. When this was being done, someone informed us that they were taking this column away, and we noticed that they were taking them to the camp. The column had almost passed through at that time. The school is here, and they were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay, sir. If -- I'm going to show you in just a moment a close-up map, a more detailed map of Mehurici, and perhaps you could use that map to assist the Trial Chamber, but let me just ask you this question, and I don't believe it's visible on this map, but you tell us: Is Kaurske Ravni, where you were positioned, visible on this map or is it actually off the map?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Kaurske Ravni can't be seen on this map. It's a little further above.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, based on your knowledge and familiarity with this area, approximately how far is it from Miletici to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: From Mehurici to Luka, well, it's exactly two kilometres from Mehurici to Luka. And then there is the route -- road that leads to Miletici. From the river, I think it's about a kilometre to up there. In the village itself there's Donji Miletici, and here we have Gornji Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But just so it's clear, from Mehurici to Luka is two kilometres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And from Luka to Miletici it's about a kilometre?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, I would ask that the witness be shown a map of Mehurici. Again, it's a further enhancement of the large mounted map which we've been using throughout these proceedings. And I do have sufficient copies. While that's being done, Mr. President, are we sitting until 12.30? Is that the time of the next technical break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. Perhaps my colleague can provide us with information. We can see a map of Orasac but not one of Miletici -- Mehurici. We have a map of Orasac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. We seem to have misdistributed a couple of maps. If the usher could take the -- that's the correct map on the ELMO. It appears as though the Defence -- I don't know about the accused but certainly the Defence have ... And perhaps again if the AV booth could zoom out a bit on this map that would be helpful. Or maybe not if it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, you have in front of you now a map of Mehurici. Let me ask you, first of all, if you recognise this portrayal of the village of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before I ask you to make any markings again with the thin, black marker, if you could take the pointer that you have and identify for us the primary school in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: That's the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if you could take the thin, black marker that the usher will provide to you and circle that, please. I take it, sir, that the SK above that, does that indicate skola or school?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, it's the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could circle the building and the identifying letters, that will help us all remember what you've -- what you've marked. So if you could please circle the school building and the letters SK.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask you this, sir: Are you familiar again, based on the amount of time that you've spent in Mehurici, with the location of the blacksmith shop?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The blacksmith's shop was used by this labour organisation called Sebesic. They would forge certain items that were necessary for tractors or for other reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know where the -- where the blacksmith shop, and again, I'm talking about 1993, the location of the blacksmith shop on this map? Is it visible? And if it is, if you could take the pointer and point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The blacksmith shop should be somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could please circle that, the building that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you could please place just immediately above that the number 1.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've also told us about a bridge in Mehurici where you saw this group of villagers being escorted by the Mujahedin. Do you see this bridge you've been referring to on the map, and if so, could you please point to it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please circle the bridge with the thin black marker and place the number 2 next to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, given the scale or the enlargement of this map, I take it that the Savici settlement is not visible on this map.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. The settlement itself should be here, further down. But Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. recently, in the 1990s, some houses were constructed in this part here, just below this little forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to again just stay if we could, sir, focused on 1993. Approximately how far is it from the bridge that you've just circled with the number 2 and the Savici settlement?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, up to the village itself where the old village is located, the distance is between 500 and 700 metres, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask that if the witness please could on the bottom right-hand corner of this map sign his name and place today's date of 2 November, 2004, on the corners, please.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, before you take that map off, actually, I did have one additional question. The columns that you saw being taken by the Mujahedin, can you, again starting with the pointer, can you point the direction that you personally observed them travelling on that day?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, when we were told that the Mujahedin were taking a column of inhabitants from the village of Miletici away, we passed by the school, and we noticed the end of the column here. There's a building located here in which there was a shop. So they passed by that area, that location, very rapidly. They continued across the bridge. And this would be the area where the camp was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if you could please take the thin, black marker and draw the line of the column as it passed by the school over the bridge and into the camp.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, please. If you could continue all the way down to where the camp was located in 1993.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. For the benefit of the -- of the record, if you could place the number 3 next to the line.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it's not clear to me, sir, but where the line stops, is that where the camp was located?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can see, yes. Perhaps it's across this road on this side, about here, because this road turns off in the direction of Poljanice, and this is the road leading to Savici. So it would be more or less in this area as far as I can see on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please circle the area of the camp and place the number 4 next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. If you could then on the first map also sign and date it on the bottom right-hand corner, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, just a couple of questions before we take the technical break. You told us that the Mujahedin moved into the Serb houses or former Serb houses in the Savici settlement, but you've also told us that the camp was in a meadow, I believe, was the word that was used in the English transcript. Can you tell you the relationship between the former Serb houses and the meadow?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was the meadow in front of the houses or what was the relationship between the houses and the meadow?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: If you're looking at it from the direction of Mehurici, the camp was before the houses themselves in the village of Savici, in the core part of the village. I said that in the 1990s, two houses were constructed and perhaps stables in the lower part, the exit from Mehurici, and I encircled the position of the camp. So they were there in the land -- on the land that belonged to the inhabitants of the village of Savici, in the lower part closer to the village of Mehurici, the settlement, the houses themselves were a little above.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, was this camp in any way enclosed such as with fences or gates, or was it simply an open meadow with some houses?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I personally never passed by the camp. I was never in the vicinity of the camp, so I don't know whether it was fenced in. There wasn't a wall around it because that would have been visible. There was no wall, because from the other side, when I went to the position via the village of Orahovo, I could see the camp from the other side, and it wasn't possible to notice walls or anything like that. As to whether there was a wire fence around it, I really don't know because I never came close to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's half past twelve. We'll have our break now, and we will resume at about five to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I have just a few remaining questions for you. I know that everyone in the courtroom would like to finish your testimony today so that you can go home, so I would ask you to keep your answers as brief as possible, and if need be, we will ask you to expand upon them. You told us earlier this morning that only a few Bosniaks went into the Mujahedin camp, and you said that they were people who had gained their trust. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I do indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any of the people that would fall into the category of those who had gained the trust of the Mujahedin and thus were allowed to go into that camp?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I remember Durmis. We all knew that he often passed that way and entered their camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: There were some people whom we used to see, and it was said that they were the ones, but I can't remember any of the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall approximately when the Mujahedin left the school in Mehurici and went to the camp or established the camp near Savici settlement?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I believe that this was sometime in autumn 1992. It was towards the end of summer or beginning of autumn 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I believe you also told us that this person whom you identified as Ramadan had been in the school, had had his office in the school in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What exactly was this person Ramadan doing in the school in Mehurici or later in the camp near Savici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: In my personal view and according to the information that I had, Ramadan was in charge of some logistical duties on behalf of the Mujahedin. He constantly moved about. And the story had it -- I don't know it personally, but the story had it that he had at his disposal a certain amount of money. So he was an important man for them from that point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did this person Ramadan -- first of all, do you know any other name, his first name or his complete name, and where this Ramadan was from?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I only know him as Ramadan. At that time, the story had it that he hailed from Jordan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did this person speak Bosnian at all?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, I had an occasion to hear him during the negotiations. He spoke the language rather well. He understood the language very well, and one could communicate with him. He did have a trace of an accent, but one could communicate with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And so I take it during the negotiations that he was in fact serving also as an interpreter for Mr. Haris, or Dr. Haris, interpreting between Bosnian and Arabic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. On several occasions he got involved in order to explain things. So, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn your attention very quickly to the column of people, including the people who later stayed in your house. These were people from Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any of those people who were part of that column that was taken by the Mujahedin and who later stayed in your house?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I remember, for example, Stipo Pavlovic and his wife; Marko Pavlovic and his wife Mara; Zdravko Pavlovic and his wife; Srecko Pavlovic; Ivo Pavlovic and his wife and one of their daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, how -- how long did these people remain in your house, and approximately when did they arrive and when did they leave?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: We brought them to my house on the 24th, sometime before midnight. They stayed in my house on the 25th, and on the 26th, in the late hours of the afternoon, they were taken by UNHCR vehicles accompanied by UNPROFOR. All of them were taken there except for the five who had decided to remain in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the five who remained in the village were the five -- I believe you told us that a platoon from the Zagradje school promised to protect those individuals who remained in Miletici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. This platoon, which was the platoon on reserve in the school, was tasked with keeping guard and protecting the village, particularly in this initial period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what happened to those five individuals who remained in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, for a certain period of time they lived there, and then they abandoned the village. Marko Pavlovic and his wife left, his wife Mara. Somewhat later on Zdravko Pavlovic and his wife left. And Srecko Pavlovic remained on his own. I can't remember exactly, but after a certain period of time, Srecko Pavlovic died.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, was there ever a time when any of the foreign Mujahedin were staying at the school in Zagradje?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. When they entered the school in Mehurici, a small group of them, maybe five or six of them, arrived in the Zagradje school. They stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When was that? Sorry. Sorry, sir. When was this that this five or six arrived in the Zagradje school?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Possibly sometime around the end of 1992. Towards the end of 1992 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long did they remain there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I think that they didn't say any longer than a month or a month and a half. They withdrew down to Mehurici. People who had contacts with them said that they had abandoned that village because the people there did not practice the true Islam, and that's why they decided to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have three last questions, sir. The first one relates to the platoon in the Zagradje school. What brigade did that platoon belong to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: That platoon belonged to the 314th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Second question, sir, you made reference several times in your testimony to the Mehurici Detachment that was in the primary school. What did you mean by the Mehurici Detachment, and what unit was that detachment a part of?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Up to the moment when the brigades were established, the organisation of the army followed detachments. Those were units established in the local communes. So the Mehurici Detachment became part of the 306th Brigade once it was established. And this was also the case with the Han Bila Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And finally, sir, for the benefit of the transcript, you also made reference to the Sipraski battalion. What brigade did that unit belong to and where was it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The Siprage Battalion, at the beginning, belonged to the 306th Brigade. Its base was in the Mehurici school. The reason for that was that the majority of the members of the battalion was made up of people who had been expelled from Kotor Varos, Skender Vakuf, Jajce, Mrkonjic Grad, and the other territories that fell under the Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I apologise, sir. I have one final question. Who in 1993 was the commander of the Sipraski Brigade -- or Battalion, rather? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The commander of the Sipraski Battalion, while it was on the strength of the 306th, was Mirza Lubenovic. That battalion was later on the core of the 27th Brigade. For the most part, it was made up of people who hailed from these municipalities on the outskirts of Travnik and somewhat further from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions this morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any re-examination on the part of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ribo, you have told the Prosecution that the Mujahedin moved around freely and that from time to time they would go to the field once you noticed them on the lines facing the Serb forces, possibly reconnoitering. Do you know maybe who ordered them to go to those areas? Did anybody from the BiH army issue any orders to them at all?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: According to the information that I had at the time and according to what I could observe and notice, they acted absolutely independently. They never consulted anybody prior to leaving. And once they were up there, they did not behave as if there was anybody up there that could issue orders or give assignments to them. I remember a case that took place in the area towards Neokrnje. When they came there there was some 30 or so of them. They were offered to take one part of the line. At first they agreed. That was before noon. And already in the afternoon, they abandoned that line and withdrew towards Mehurici. And I remember well --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have said that they very rarely took part in combat. Did you ever see them engaged in combat together with the members of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I personally never saw them in any combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, can you please tell me, when you were talking about some local Muslims and particularly refugees from the general area, for the reasons that you have explained to the Honourable Chamber, approached the Mujahedin, and some of them joined them. Were you ever in your position, in your capacity as a soldier, to estimate the strength that they had at their disposal in the camp or in the area that they were moving about?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Objectively speaking, I personally could not arrive at an estimate of their real strength.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also told us that you could see them passing by in a Toyota, and there were about eight to ten of them standing in the vehicle. Could you observe the kind of weapons that they had? With regard to the weapons that the BiH army had at the time, can you tell us what kind of weapons they had in terms of quality? Was -- was it better or worse?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: From the time that they first appeared, they had at their disposal much better arms, much modern arms than members of the army had in that area. I personally noticed that they had automatic rifles. They had Zoljas. Many of them had Zoljas and Osas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question to you, Mr. Ribo, related to the way they recruited locals. Did it happen that some of them married girls from your area or from the refugee families, and this was done in a very strange way?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. This was a very conspicuous thing, a very visible thing. A certain number of very young girls, which is unusual, and it didn't have a positive reaction with the locals. They abused the poverty of some of the families, especially the families that lived in austerity or came from the ranks of refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Ribo. Mr. President, I don't have any further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have a couple of questions with regard to what my learned friend asked him on the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ribo, on the map that the Prosecutor showed to you you circled the village of Zagradje.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I circled the village of Luka. The settlement of Zagradje remained beyond that circle. On that particular map one can't see the whole of that settlement. I'm talking about Luka village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Zagradje?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It is in the municipality of Travnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify some things. Is the school in Zagradje or Luka?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: It's in Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So the village of Zagradje doesn't have a school?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The school was built as the focal point for a number of settlements among which Miletici, Skomorje, Zagradje, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This village Zagradje that belongs to the municipality of Travnik, in the months of April, May, and the summer of 1993, did it have anything Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to do with the 309th Brigade from Kakanj or the TO from Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No. According to my information, this is not the case. I have not heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it's not in the transcript that it's the 309th Brigade from Kakanj. Could you please correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You're a geography teacher. Could you please tell us or do you know, for example, that there is also a Zagradje village in the municipality of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that there -- that it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown document P564? I have a copy of the document here. If you permit me, Mr. President, to save time, I would just like to present that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document, and this is an order of the 7th Muslim Brigade, where a company from the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Brigade, which was located in Kakanj, is being sent to the school in the village of Zagradje. Could you please look at item 5 of this order, which states that the commander of the 3rd Battalion will inform the commander of the 309th Brigade about the implementation of this order. Have you read the document? Would you agree with me, Mr. Ribo, that this order that you are looking at does not refer to the village of Zagradje in the Travnik municipality precisely for the reasons that I mentioned, and because of your answer?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. The contents indicate -- do not indicate that village that I talked about is the village that is discussed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree would me that this refers to the entire of Zagradje in the municipality of Kakanj in view of item 5, which speaks about the Kakanj Brigade and the Kakanj municipality TO?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear here. It is very specifically stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few questions for you, sir. These questions arise from what you have stated on the page 105 to the Defence question. You responded that on a certain day, you saw the arrival of some 30 Mujahedin, and they left in the afternoon. As far as you can remember, can you tell us whether -- when was it? Which year and which month did this happen?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I can say that this way in which they moved was something that happened quite often. You could even say that this happened each month. They were always going off somewhere. Where and what they were doing, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but only the day when you saw them, you told us that you saw that some 30 of them had arrived. You even indicated the place. When was it? On what date?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I will try to remember. I think that this was sometime at the beginning of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was in October 1992. How many of you were there on the spot?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I personally was there in reconnaissance and in order to determine certain targets for the howitzer, for our weapons to be fired at Serb positions. So that is what I was doing up there. So I was working on this specific task, and as I was doing that, I noticed that this group of Mujahedin arrived, and that is how I learned that perhaps they were supposed to stay there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when you were there and you were reconnoitering, there were Serbs on the other side of the line. Were there any other people? Was there a superior commander there, somebody you reported to.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No. My commander was actually in Travnik. I was given the assignment of going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were on your own. And you had the only -- you were the only person with authority on that spot?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I was with the howitzer platoon commander. Together with him I was there that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: His name is Sead Zukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when this commander saw the arrival of 30 persons, did he find that normal? Did he talk to them? What happened?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: We were surprised in a way, because they just happened to appear there at that point. So we didn't have an opportunity of engaging into any kind of conversation or communication with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So nobody talked to them. They just arrived. You are contradicting yourself, because you said that they were asked to do something, they did it, but they abandoned the position in the afternoon. So there must have been some sort of a conversation between them and yourselves.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No. My commander, Zukic, and I did not have any conversations with them because we had our own specific assignment. We were there to carry out this assignment. When we were supposed to go back to our positions, in a conversation with the people of a unit from the settlement of Gluha Bukovica, we learned that they had arrived and that it was a question of whether they would stay or not, and then tomorrow, the next day, we found out that that same day, late in the afternoon, they returned on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You saw them with your own two eyes or not? Did you see them? Did you physically see these people?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were they armed? Did they wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed. They were in uniforms. And also, all of them had their traditional garb over their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the distance between yourselves and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: The place where we were reconnoitering in relation to the Serbs was about 1.5 to 2 kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you were observing the Serbs, did you have binoculars?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Serbs, did they have binoculars?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: They probably did. It could be assumed that they had the best and the most modern equipment that was in the possession of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were the Serbs in the position to observe these 30 individuals?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that, because the area where they had come to was on a slope behind a wood. They were in that place. We happened to be at an elevation from where we had a good view of the Serb lines ahead of us, and they were, in a way, located at that point in time to our rear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: To pursue your remarks on this subject, Witness, you also mentioned some minutes ago something you saw in a place called Neokrnje. Could you tell us what you wanted to tell us about that place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I apologise. This place that you mentioned, I'm not sure what it is. What place exactly is it? In which context is it being mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, let me recall that you wanted to give an example of the intervention of Mujahedin in a battle situation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone, please, for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Some 20 minutes or ten minutes ago you said -- you wanted to give an example of participating of Mujahedin in combat situations, and you mentioned a place which I noted was Neokrnje or something like that. As an example that they never --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: Neokrnje. That's the place you mean. Yes, yes. That is a police in this area that I spoke about where I was on that day, in reconnaissance. If we look in front of us, that place is to our left, and the places of the Serb forces are to the right, towards Teslic. At the time, that place was controlled by the Serbs, and we were reconnoitering in that sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And why did you mention this place? What would you -- were you intending to illustrate with your reference to this place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: That was an important strategic place for our units, because I can say at the same time that that hill, that mountain of Neokrnje, was the last land belonging to the Bosniaks in that section towards the municipalities of Kotor Varos and Teslic. So normally it was in the interest -- in our interest to hold onto that place because it had a special strategic importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And what did it have to do with the Mujahedin then?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: I don't know. I just mentioned that at the time when we were in reconnaissance, they happened to arrive there from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to put you a very different question on the events in Miletici. You spoke with Abu Haris, I understand, and you spoke with Ramadan. You had negotiations. In these talks, did they ever tell you or did they ever explain you why they went to Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: No. I didn't have the opportunity of talking to any of them about that matter. I was never in a position to specifically talk about the -- their motives for going to Miletici. At the negotiations themselves, in a conversation I told Ramadan that we, the population, the Bosniaks, if necessary, could deal with these citizens if we were suspecting them of doing anything against the army. That was the only dialogue that I had with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from other persons an explanation for their -- their going to Miletici? I mean, not for the shooting. That is evident. But the reason why they went to Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN RIBO
utterances.text: At one time in a conversation, some of them spoke about it as if it was something that they did because of the events in Ahmici. This is what I heard, but I didn't hear anything else more specific in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any questions? We have a few minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your testimony is now finished. We would like to thank you for coming to The Hague to answer the questions put to you by the Defence, the Prosecution, and the Judges. We wish you a happy journey back home, and we also wish you success in your career. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to deal with the admission of documents. The Defence had one document to tender.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we tender our document marked on our list and presented to the witness under number 0586 into evidence because the witness recognised this document as coming from his brigade. He recognised the person who signed this document. And from personal experience, he notes that the facts mentioned in this document reflect the situation in January 1993. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No -- no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you give us a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document will be admitted as DH586, and the English version will be DH586/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Prosecution, any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all respect, we would respectfully request that the two maps that were marked by the witness be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two maps. One map, a general map, and one map which depicts Mehurici. Mr. Registrar, can we have numbers? Defence, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Registrar, can we have two numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first number, the first map is admitted as P933, and the other map depicting Mehurici will be P934.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'm turning towards the Defence to hear the schedule for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as we said on Friday and also yesterday, we cannot bring any witnesses for tomorrow. And for Thursday we have two witnesses and another witness for Friday. The Victims and Witnesses Unit did not manage until today -- actually, they managed to get a visa for these three witnesses only today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. In that case, although we had scheduled a sitting for tomorrow, it has to be cancelled. Any other issues to raise at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the Defence is in a position to inform us as to the witnesses for next week, we would certainly appreciate that in light of the fact that we aren't sitting tomorrow, because if we only find out on Thursday or Friday, we may have difficulties with respect to next week's schedule. So if they are in a position to inform us whose coming next week, we would certainly appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will provide our learned colleagues with a list of witnesses for next week tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is the time to wrap up. I thank you, and I invite you to come back not tomorrow but the day after tomorrow. Our sitting will start at 9.00 in the morning.
